_comment: Tolerances for `tools/logcmp.py` on the STOCK vs ff_fuel-at-E0 comparison
(docs/05_flexfuel_design.md section 6 'E0 equivalence', docs/06 section 7).
At E0 the patch is supposed to change NOTHING: ff_f_q10 is 1024 and
ff_rk_scale() takes its early return without writing 0x803038 at all. That
is proved exactly in the emulator
(tests/test_ff_fuel_patch.py::TestRkStub::test_f_1024_leaves_rk_untouched);
on the bench the two runs are separate drives of the same scenario, so
every number below is run-to-run repeatability of the ECU, NOT a budget the
patch may spend. A deviation inside these limits does not prove the patch
is innocent - it only fails to prove it guilty.
Use this file for the E0 run only. For a blended run (E20/E50/E85) the
fuelling signals are SUPPOSED to move, and comparing them against a
gasoline baseline is meaningless; procedure.md section 6 says what to
check instead.
CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (E4/E5): the ff_* variables are NOT absent from the
stock log. The session file reads them as plain RAM addresses, so on a
stock image they are whatever that RAM holds - in practice 0 - and logcmp
compares them like anything else. They are therefore listed below with
NULL limits, which is this file's way of saying 'expected to differ, do
not judge': a stock-vs-patched comparison of ff_e_filt is meaningless, but
the variable still has to appear so that a reader can see it was
considered rather than forgotten. The same treatment goes to the raster
counters, which start at a different power-up offset in every run (see the
alignment step in procedure.md section 4).
These limits are a STARTING POINT from the signals' idle behaviour, not
from two recorded runs. Record two stock runs first and tighten every line
to what the ECU actually repeats; a tolerance wider than the repeatability
proves nothing.

rk_fuel_mass._unit: counts, u16, 0x803038; THE signal of this patch. At E0 the patched code never writes it, so the only spread here is the ECU's own cycle-to-cycle variation

ti_sum._unit: us, 1 us/LSB, u16 0x8030C4 (injection.md section 8, rail.md section 11); was 0.4/0.1 ms while the session file still carried the 4-byte ms definition (fixed 2026-09-17)

prist_w._unit: bar, 0.005/LSB, 0x8031DA; rail ripple at idle dominates. It must also stay ABOVE 13 bar in absolute terms (rail.md section 14)

dwi_inj_angle._unit: degCA, 0x803088; the injection-window signal, rises with rk

fr_bank_a._unit: -, Q15 1.0 = 32768, 0x802DF8, measuring id 29, VCDS 001.3. The closed-loop lambda factor: at E0 it must sit where it sat on stock

frm_bank_a._unit: -, Q15, 0x801E36, measuring id 33, VCDS 032.2. Multiplicative adaptation; it moves slowly, so a step here is the first sign the patch changed fuelling

dwkrz_0._note: 2026-09-22 wave-F integration: max_abs raised from 0.75 (one LSB) to 1.5 (two LSB). dwkrz is an integer staircase; two separately sampled runs interpolated across a step edge differ by exactly one LSB, which failed logcmp stock-vs-E0 in bench_rehearsal.py about 1 run in 3 (brief F3 report). Retighten from two real stock runs with logcmp.py derive.
dwkrz_0._unit: degCA, 0.75/LSB, 0x7FCE57; per-cylinder knock retard, ONE ROW EACH because a single cylinder is what knocks. At E0 with ff_zw_enable = 0 the patch adds no advance at all, so any step here is the ECU's own run-to-run knock behaviour - but a systematic move on one cylinder is the first thing to look at (ignition.md section 6)

wkrm._unit: degCA, 0.75/LSB, 0x7FCE76; the MEAN knock retard, the input of the stock low-octane detector. It has to repeat at E0

zw_low_octane_latch._unit: -, 0x7FD31B & 3; the stock low-octane latch. It must be IDENTICAL, and in practice 0, in both runs: a bit set on the patched run only would mean the patch changed the ignition at E0, which it must not

rl_w._unit: %, 100/4096 per LSB, 0x7FEFB2; the KFZW column-axis input the blend reads. E1 found this is rl_w - 0x7FED38 is rl_for_fuel, a different cell

eep_blk8_mirror_b0._unit: -, 0x7F9F80; the EEP_CONF block 8 BLOCK ID byte. It must be 0x08 in both runs and never move: a mismatch makes nvm_read_all_blocks discard the block (eeprom.md section 10.5)

eep_blk8_mirror_b1._unit: -, 0x7F9F81; the VERSION byte of the same stamp. Same rule

eep_blk8_mirror_b2._unit: %, 0x7F9F82; WHERE THE PATCH STORES the ethanol estimate since the E4 correction (ff_persist_offset = 2). It is 0xFF or a stale value on the stock run and the current estimate on the patched one, so it cannot be compared - check it against ff_e_persist instead (procedure_d2.md B2)

eep_blk8_mirror_b14._unit: -, 0x7F9F8E; the ONE byte stock code writes (call site 0x134380). The patch must never move it, in either run

eep_blk8_mirror_b29._unit: -, 0x7F9F9D; the manager's own ReplV byte. It MOVES on the first commit (0xFF -> 0x00 -> 0x01), so it differs between a run that committed and one that did not. The rule is 'the patch never writes it', which is asserted in the emulator, not on this line (eeprom.md 10.6)

eep_blk8_mirror_csum._unit: -, 0x7F9F9E; the block checksum. It follows every payload change, so it differs whenever the patched run committed. What has to hold is the INVARIANT sum(+0..+29) + csum == 0xFFFF in every sample of both runs, which logcmp cannot express - procedure_d2.md B2 checks it

nvm_queue_state._unit: -, 0x7FADAB; the block manager's queue state. It is 0x20/0x21 in both runs but steps through other values whenever a commit is in flight, which only the patched run does

raster_setA_10ms_count._unit: count, 0x7FD754; EXCLUDED ON PURPOSE. These are free-running counters whose value depends on how long the ECU has been powered before the log starts, so a stock-vs-patched difference means nothing. They are the ALIGNMENT signal instead: procedure.md section 4 shifts the candidate log by (raster_cand - raster_base) / 100 s before logcmp runs. What must hold is the SLOPE, about 100 counts per second

raster_setB_10ms_count._unit: count, 0x7FD758; EXCLUDED ON PURPOSE. These are free-running counters whose value depends on how long the ECU has been powered before the log starts, so a stock-vs-patched difference means nothing. They are the ALIGNMENT signal instead: procedure.md section 4 shifts the candidate log by (raster_cand - raster_base) / 100 s before logcmp runs. What must hold is the SLOPE, about 100 counts per second

raster_setB_1ms_count._unit: count, 0x7FD760; EXCLUDED ON PURPOSE. These are free-running counters whose value depends on how long the ECU has been powered before the log starts, so a stock-vs-patched difference means nothing. They are the ALIGNMENT signal instead: procedure.md section 4 shifts the candidate log by (raster_cand - raster_base) / 100 s before logcmp runs. What must hold is the SLOPE, about 100 counts per second

can_rx_spare0_b0._unit: %, 0x803F9C; byte 0 of the Pico frame in the driver shadow. Nothing writes it on a stock image, so it is 0 there and the raw ethanol percent on the patched one

can_rx_spare0_ctr._unit: -, 0x803F9F; byte 3, the Pico's rolling counter. Same reason

tmst._unit: degC, 0.75/LSB -48, 0x8021F6; latched at start, so it only differs if the two runs started at different coolant temperatures - which is worth knowing

ksta_adapted._unit: -, Q10 1024 = 1.00x, 0x80302C; the cranking lever, and the cell E2's two S1 stubs publish. At E0 with ff_st_enable = 0 it must be IDENTICAL - this is the E0 proof for the start half, and outside the start it is pinned at 0x400 in both runs

zwstt._unit: degCA, 0.75/LSB, 0x802096; the start ignition angle E2's Z1 stub publishes. Identical at E0, same argument, and it matters more than most: the knock retard is BYPASSED during the start

B_st._unit: -, 0x7FE91D; start attempt active. A start-phase signal: the two runs are separate drives and their starts do not line up in time, so a sample-by-sample comparison is meaningless. Compare the start SERIES against anztist / zdgz instead (procedure_e2.md B3)

B_stend._unit: -, 0x7FE921; start finished; THE gate of both S1 stubs. A start-phase signal: the two runs are separate drives and their starts do not line up in time, so a sample-by-sample comparison is meaningless. Compare the start SERIES against anztist / zdgz instead (procedure_e2.md B3)

anztist._unit: -, 0x7FD269; injections since start. A start-phase signal: the two runs are separate drives and their starts do not line up in time, so a sample-by-sample comparison is meaningless. Compare the start SERIES against anztist / zdgz instead (procedure_e2.md B3)

zdgz._unit: -, 0x7FCE14; ignitions since start. A start-phase signal: the two runs are separate drives and their starts do not line up in time, so a sample-by-sample comparison is meaningless. Compare the start SERIES against anztist / zdgz instead (procedure_e2.md B3)

tnst_w._unit: -, 0x8011D8; the after-start timer. A start-phase signal: the two runs are separate drives and their starts do not line up in time, so a sample-by-sample comparison is meaningless. Compare the start SERIES against anztist / zdgz instead (procedure_e2.md B3)

fr_w_b1._unit: -, Q15 1.0 = 32768, 0x802DF8; the bank-1 lambda correction. Clamped out of the loop during the start, so this is a POST-start signal; at E0 it must settle where it settled on stock

rlsol_req._unit: %, 100/32768 per LSB, 0x803510, measuring id 375; the charge REQUEST. It is what a start or a window limit has to be read against, and at E0 the same drive must ask for the same thing

rl_max_arb._unit: %, 100/65536 per LSB, 0x80235A, measuring id 2051; the ARBITRATED charge limit. Normally 0xFFFF; anything lower on the patched run only would mean a limiter armed that did not arm on stock

prsoll_raw._unit: bar, 0.005/LSB, 0x8031F0; the cell E5's stub publishes. At E0 with ff_prail_enable = 0 it must be BIT-IDENTICAL, not close: the stub stores the same halfword the stock sth would have. This line is the E0 proof for the rail half

prsoll_clamped._unit: bar, 0.005/LSB, 0x8031F2; prsoll_raw after PRSOLMN and KLPRMAX. Identical at E0, and in ABSOLUTE terms it may never exceed 22000 counts = 110.0 bar in either run

prsoll_rate._unit: bar, 0.005/LSB, 0x8031EE; after the pump-volume rate limiter. Identical at E0

prsoll_w._unit: bar, 0.005/LSB, 0x8031F4, measuring id 501; the setpoint the controller works to. Identical at E0

prdiff._unit: bar, 0.005/LSB, 0x8031CA, measuring id 1691; prsoll - prist. Rail ripple dominates, as it does for prist_w. A systematic positive shift on the patched run is 'the pump cannot follow'

vhdp_spare._unit: -, 0x8031F6; spare pump volume. Noisy, but it may never sit at 0 in either run - that is an absolute check, not a comparison

vmsv_limited._unit: -, 0x80316E; the MSV volume request after the VMSVMX clamp. The number that matters is absolute: pinned at 5000 means the pump is saturated

wbho1s_w._unit: degCA, 3/128 per LSB, 0x80307E; start of injection. No stock measuring id, so this needs the DDLI route. It must repeat at E0

win_margin_req._unit: 0.75 degCA per count, 0x7FD290; the required end-of-injection margin awea_angles writes from KLWBHO1SMX. A calibration-driven constant (67 in this dataset): it must be identical in both runs

ff_magic._unit: -, 0x7FFB00; a patch state-block field. It reads 0 on a stock image (the address is plain RAM there), so a stock-vs-patched comparison says nothing. Judge it against emu/models/flexfuel.py and the procedures instead

_open: fra, the ADDITIVE lambda adaptation at 0x801D1A (injection.md section 9),
has no measuring id in re/measuring_vars.csv, so it can only be logged over
the DDLI route. Add it to the session file as a u16 at 0x801D1A once the
logger of #20 is on the bench; its Q15 scaling is inferred from the same
instruction that adds it, not measured.
The lambda SENSOR signal itself (lamson / lamsoni in FR terms) has not been
located in re/measuring_vars.csv: the handler table has 665 implemented ids
and none of them is named for it yet (re/findings/measuring_vars.md
section 6 lists this as the quickest open route). The wideband in the
exhaust is the substitute for the blended runs of procedure.md section 6,
and it is the instrument that matters there anyway.
